candidates.snrConditions: 0–5 V unipolar, low-bandwidth mode, no oversampling, 1 kHz sine, 1 MSPS; sine amplitude not stated in table.
candidates.stockObserved: Search result: 130; the subsequently opened EU page says restricted availability/region restriction. Do not promise availability.

candidates.analogFilter: Third-order Butterworth; shared range selection should match all force/acceleration channels.
candidates.snrConditions: ±5 V, no oversampling, −0.5 dBFS 1 kHz sine, 200 kSPS.
candidates.simulationAdvice: Add the actual third-order 16 kHz pre-sampling response, late ADC noise and 16-bit quantization. Centered acceleration gain 2 preserves sensor range; gain 4 improves resolution but reduces range to ±31.25 g. Keep proper instrumentation amplification and the selected external filter separate.
candidates.offsetDriftInterpretation: Assume ppm of the 10 V total span: 30 uV/C. The resulting acceleration drift at conditioning gain 2 is 0.00367749375 m/s2/C. This is an analytical worst-bound mapping, not a measured thermal result.
candidates.analogResponseMatchingUnknown: The electrical table does not specify a maximum channel-to-channel analog filter delay mismatch. Measure and identify assembled paths.
candidates.groupDelaySpecificationStatus: Typical design simulation value, not a guaranteed maximum.

candidates.role: Lowest-cost plausible simultaneous architecture; native Sinc3 must be simulated
candidates.filter: Exact third-order CIC/Sinc3 at OSR128/256/512/1024; global-chop disabled. It is a modulator-clock FIR followed by decimation, not a first-order output-rate RC.
candidates.snrConditions: Typical shorted-input noise at 25°C, 3 V AVDD, internal 1.2 V reference and 8.192 MHz MCLK; use the OSR-selected table. No minimum-noise guarantee.
candidates.simulationAdvice: Use proper IA outputs into PGA1 with centered gain 0.5 for ADXL1002. Noise is already output-conditioned by the ADC's Sinc3. Do not apply the same Sinc3 again to its quoted RMS noise. A 7.68 MHz clock gives 30 ksample/s output and a synchronous 10 kHz controller. Sweep genuine 15 ksample/s and 7.5 ksample/s variants with their longer filter delay; downsampling 30 ksample/s data does not reproduce those settings.
candidates.startupAdvice: Discard unsettled first samples and establish loaded equilibrium before control; manufacturer startup/resynchronization wait is separate from steady-state filter group delay.
candidates.PGA_CommonModeNote: For PGA gains at least 8, each absolute input must be at most AVDD minus 1.8 V. Proper IA and PGA1 level shifting avoid requiring a direct 5 V excited bridge connection.
candidates.offsetDriftMapping: At centered acceleration gain 0.5, typical ADC-only drift is 0.0001054214875 m/s2/C. Whole-chain residual accuracy and temperature performance remain unqualified.

candidates.role: Multiplexed SAR comparison; requires channel timestamp reconstruction
candidates.simulationAdvice: The 500 kSPS rate is aggregate, giving 62.5 kSPS per channel for eight uniform channels. Model individual timestamps and calibrated bridge-matrix assembly. At the maximum clock, 14 us first-to-last skew implies approximately 0.010752 N analytical inertial timing error at S = 2 kg and jerk = 384 m/s3, before the feedback response. Its cost is approximately the same as ADS8588S, which is the stronger primary candidate.

forceBridgeMapping.illustrationOnly: For an effective ±160 N axis mapped to ±5 V, sensitivity is 31.25 mV/N and the 16-bit quantum is 0.0048828125 N. The six-bridge calibration matrix is not supplied; actual gains and calibration must establish equivalent noise and headroom.

frontEndCostContext.userAssumption: A proper instrumentation amplifier with a chosen analog cutoff is available. Gain, level shift and filtering are design choices.
frontEndCostContext.filterAmpIllustration: OPA1656IDR dual operational amplifier, observed at €2.57 for quantity 1 and €1.93 for quantity 10. Several packages are needed for six force and two acceleration filters. This is not a finished front-end price.
frontEndCostContext.costInference: Approximately €40 for bridge amplifiers plus €10–15 for several dual filter/conditioning amplifiers, before precision passives, reference/excitation, protection, regulators, PCB, connectors and testing. This is engineering cost context, not a purchasing list or complete BOM. The front end is mostly common to the ADC architectures; chip savings do not equal whole-system savings.

rejectedShortcuts: An 18-bit label does not guarantee 18-bit noise or accuracy. Translate the actual range, SNR and delay.
The maximum ADC rate differs from the required chosen rate. Slower output from internal oversampling adds delay and filtering.
Inject ADC intrinsic noise after the external analog filter, which precedes its generation.
ADS131M08 quoted output RMS noise already contains its Sinc3 filtering.
SAR SNR already contains quantization. Counting it again requires an explicitly conservative noise budget.
ADXL1002's 11 kHz response point is not a specified first-order lowpass pole.
Higher accelerometer gain improves ADC noise and resolution but can clip powered-sander vibration. Bump acceleration does not prove vibration headroom.
Eight-channel multiplexing at 500 kSPS aggregate gives neither 500 kSPS per channel nor simultaneous measurement.
The load-cell calibration matrix needs all six raw bridge channels. A planar controller still needs eight analog channels with two acceleration axes.

STM32H7's 16-bit register differs from effective resolution. AN5354 reports typical 12.8 single-ended and 13.7 differential effective bits. Three ADCs with multiplexing and board noise form a separate architecture requiring hardware qualification.

noiseModelCaveats: Published integrated ADC noise does not establish its sample autocorrelation at the chosen raw rate. Treating the entire RMS as independent white noise and reducing it through an EMA can be optimistic.
For SAR models, use the internal analog noise response and a separate quantizer, or retain a conservative late-noise case preserving the quoted RMS after conditioning.
ADC SNR contains quantization noise. The recipe reports both total SNR-equivalent noise and the remainder after subtracting ideal quantization variance.
M08 noise is already conditioned by the internal Sinc3. A second application of that filter to the quoted RMS understates the noise.
Typical SAR SNR is specified at the datasheet test rate, not a noise guarantee at every proposed lower rate.
